newsitem.title: USA: NHL-RANGERS LOSE LEFT WING BERG WITH BROKEN LEG.
newsitem.headline: NHL-RANGERS LOSE LEFT WING BERG WITH BROKEN LEG.

text.p: New York Rangers left wing Bill Berg suffered a fractured right leg in Tuesday's 4-3 playoff overtime victory over the Florida Panthers and will be sidelined indefinitely, the club said on Wednesday.

The injury occured in overtime. Berg and Florida centre Kirk Muller were battling for the puck in the Rangers zone when Berg went down. His right foot landed awkwardly in a rut in the ice and his ankle remained pinned under him as he fell.
New York coach Colin Campbell accused Muller of a dirty play.

"It's a tough game, survival of the fittest, but a 'slow foot' should not be allowed," said Campbell. "A slow foot is when a guy drags his foot and pulls a guy out. It's a dangerous play, a guy can fall on his head or what happened to our guy, Bill Berg...
"Muller slow-footed him. That's the worst play."
Campbell continued: "I'd rather be speared or punched in the face than slow-footed. Now we lose a player because of an irresponsible play..."
The 29-year-old Berg is one of the Rangers' top checkers. He had eight goals and six assists in 67 games during the regular season.
The Rangers lead the best-of-seven series 2-1. Game Four is Wednesday night in New York.
